title: Verifier‑Assisted versus One‑Shot LLM Intent→Configuration: A Paired NetOpsTraceBench Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed NetOpsTraceBench (study_id rX4f7-1), a paired comparison of a one‑shot NL→configuration pipeline and a verifier‑assisted generate–validate–repair pipeline using a shared initial candidate design. Using the requested model gpt-5-mini, a deterministic NetOps validator, and Mininet‑style emulation, we applied a preregistered binary episode success rule (validator accepts final config AND emulator shows no availability degradation above tolerance AND no automatic rollback). Of 1,200 planned paired tasks we completed 1,199 pairs. Baseline successes = 1,196/1,199 (0.9974979149291076); guarded successes = 1,199/1,199 (1.0). The paired success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002502085070892446 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.005838198498748957]; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis H3 (per‑cluster inferential breakdown) was not executed; only the pooled paired analysis is archived (see analysis/results.json and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Provider audit shows model_calls_used = 1,203 and repair calls = 3. Under these controlled corpus and verifier settings we find no statistically significant advantage for the verifier‑assisted pipeline; limited headroom (near‑ceiling baseline) and low repair invocation explain the null result. All run artifacts, logs, and analysis code are archived for reproducibility.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent expressed in natural language into executable device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Prior surveys and system papers emphasize that operational reliability depends on the orchestration and verification stack (model + verifier + provenance + sandboxed execution) rather than on an LLM alone [1,2]. Generate–validate–repair (verifier‑assisted) architectures are a canonical mitigation strategy: an LLM proposes candidate outputs, an automated verifier checks constraints and safety, and an automated repair loop iterates until the candidate satisfies verifier rules [3–6].

We designed NetOpsTraceBench to provide a preregistered, workflow‑centered paired comparison between (A) baseline one‑shot NL→config generation and (B) a guarded generate–validate–repair pipeline that shares an identical initial candidate per pair. The primary confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (study_id rX4f7-1). The study preregistration froze inclusion/exclusion rules, seeds, stopping rules, analysis code, and a binary rollback‑aware episode success metric prior to model interaction (preregistration SHA‑256 = 77abe8b493bde44484e0b3d02cfd7f9ec1621ff7e7847889082ae177a7ed5712).

Note on preregistered topology breakdown (H3): the plan included a confirmatory topology‑cluster breakdown (edge vs core) as H3. That per‑cluster inferential analysis was not executed; only the pooled paired analysis was performed and archived. We explicitly disclose this here and point readers to the archived pooled analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) and the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) that document the completed run and accounting. Manuscript wording has been corrected to avoid implying that H3 was performed.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and system papers frame LLMs as components inside broader AIOps/NetOps workflows and call for workflow‑centered evaluation—trace quality, validator interactions, emulator execution, and rollback‑aware metrics—rather than isolated one‑shot QA tests [1,2,4]. Verifier‑assisted and generate–validate‑repair patterns appear in NL→formal translation, topology compilation, and configuration‑repair prototypes; these works report feasibility and localized gains but also emphasize sensitivity to task selection and verifier design [5–10].

Empirical studies catalog LLM failure modes (hallucination, unit/semantic errors, overconfidence/miscalibration, prompt‑injection) that motivate external verification and provenance linking; several demonstrations show verifier‑guided repair reduces some classes of syntactic/semantic errors in constrained settings, but generality remains open [11–14]. The literature therefore motivates a preregistered, artifact‑rich paired evaluation that records provider traces, validator diagnostics, and emulator outcomes so that the effect of verifier design and task corpus can be examined reproducibly. NetOpsTraceBench implements these recommendations and publishes the analysis artifacts used for inference.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand: NetOpsTraceBench (rX4f7-1) preregistered confirmatory hypotheses (H1–H3), inclusion/exclusion rules, frozen seeds, the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), a power rationale (MDE = 5 percentage points under baseline ≈ 0.70), and an analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The preregistration manifest SHA‑256 is 77abe8b493bde44484e0b3d02cfd7f9ec1621ff7e7847889082ae177a7ed5712.

Task corpus and pipeline semantics: The benchmark generated 1,200 deterministic intent→config tasks (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, generator_version = 5.0) split conceptually into two topology clusters (edge = 600, core = 600) and labeled each task with difficulty metadata. Each task pair used shared_initial_candidate semantics (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate") so baseline and guarded episodes start from the same LLM candidate, isolating the verifier/repair effect. The requested_model was gpt-5-mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; model configuration archive records requested_model = gpt-5-mini and max_output_tokens = 1500.

Baseline and guarded conditions: Baseline recorded the shared initial candidate and proceeded to deterministic parsing and emulator checks without invoking repair. Guarded fed the same shared initial candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0); on rejection the guarded pipeline could invoke a single preregistered repair call (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). All provider calls, repair prompts, validator traces, and scoring artifacts were archived.

Binary episode success and exclusions: The preregistered binary episode success required (a) validator acceptance of the final configuration (validation_after.valid == true), (b) emulator execution showing no availability degradation beyond tolerance, and (c) no automatic rollback during execution. Deterministic exclusion rules (contamination thresholds, parse failures, emulator measurement failures) were applied automatically and logged; no human adjudication occurred. The missingness plan defined primary analysis as complete_pair_primary (exclude flagged pairs) with a sensitivity analysis treating excluded pairs as failures.

Note on H3 (topology‑cluster breakdown): H3 was preregistered as a confirmatory per‑cluster breakdown. The archived evidence contains only the pooled paired analysis; per‑cluster inferential artifacts were not produced. The pooled analysis artifacts and execution accounting are archived at analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, and execution/execution_manifest.json. This manuscript corrects prior phrasing that implied H3 had been performed and explicitly reports that only pooled inference is available.
sections.results:
Execution summary and accounting: The run completed 2,398 of 2,400 planned episodes, producing 1,199 complete paired observations (complete_pair_count = 1,199). Provider audit records hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,203 and model_calls_used = 1,203; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,202 and failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1. Stage_counts reveal shared_initial_generation = 1,200 and repair = 3, i.e., automated repair was invoked in exactly three episodes.

Primary paired outcomes (pooled): The 2×2 paired contingency counts are n11 = 1,196 (both succeeded), n10 = 3 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). From these counts: baseline_success_count = 1,196 (baseline_success_rate = 1,196/1,199 = 0.9974979149291076) and guarded_success_count = 1,199 (guarded_success_rate = 1,199/1,199 = 1.0). The observed paired‑success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002502085070892446.

Confirmatory inference and CI: Because outcomes are binary and discordant pairs are few, the archived confirmatory analysis executed an exact McNemar two‑sided test on (n10, n01) and computed a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). The exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25 and the 95% bootstrap CI for the paired‑success‑rate difference is [0.0000, 0.005838198498748957]. These results and the bootstrap parameters are archived in analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Missingness and exclusions: analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 1,199, failed_baseline_episodes = 1, failed_guarded_episodes = 1, and both_missing_pairs = 1. Contamination checks did not trigger deterministic exclusions (analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty). The single dropped pair accounts for the planned 1,200 → observed 1,199 complete pairs.

Representative validator traces and repair diagnostics: Representative per‑episode scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json etc.) show that validation_after.valid == true and repair_applied == false for the majority of episodes; the repair stage was exercised only three times (repair = 3). These archived traces (execution/scoring/*.json) illustrate that under the chosen deterministic task generator and validator settings the initial LLM shared candidate frequently satisfied intent constraints, materially limiting repair invocation.
sections.discussion:
Statistical and operational interpretation: The pooled inference shows no statistically significant advantage for the guarded pipeline under the supplied corpus and validator settings (exact McNemar p = 0.25; 95% CI includes zero). Two artifact‑grounded factors explain this null finding. First, baseline performance was near ceiling (≈99.75%), which drastically reduces absolute headroom for improvement; the preregistered MDE (5 percentage points) assumed a much lower baseline and thus the run was underpowered to detect the observed ≈0.25 percentage‑point gain. Second, repair invocation was rare (repair = 3), because deterministic task generation and validator configuration produced initial candidates that the validator accepted in the vast majority of episodes. Provider audit (model_calls_used = 1,203; stage_counts repair = 3) and per‑episode validator traces support both points.

Shared_initial_candidate design rationale: We used a shared_initial_candidate paired design (both conditions start from the same LLM candidate) to isolate the verifier and repair effect from generation variability. The execution manifest and provider audit confirm that one shared initial generation was produced per task (shared_initial_generation = 1,200) and that observed differences arise only from the guarded pipeline's validation/repair stage. This design reduces variance attributable to stochastic generation but also reduces opportunities for guarded pipelines to improve over diverse alternative initial candidates; both tradeoffs are relevant for external validity and should guide future benchmark choices.

Threats to validity and externality: Internal validity benefits from deterministic seeds, generator, and validator components, but construct validity depends on whether our binary success rule maps to operational safety in production. External validity is limited: only the requested_model = gpt-5-mini was exercised, tasks were synthetic/consented and vendor‑agnostic, and Mininet‑style emulation may not capture vendor idiosyncrasies and transient convergence phenomena. Crucially, the preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory breakdown (H3) was not executed; only pooled inference is available (see analysis/results.json). Thus conclusions should be interpreted as conditional on corpus design and verifier settings.

Operational implications and next steps: When initial generation already meets deterministic verifier criteria for well‑specified synthetic tasks, verifier scaffolding will be infrequently exercised and measured gains on a binary success metric may be vanishingly small. To better quantify verifier value, future runs should (a) increase task ambiguity and adversarial content, (b) vary verifier strictness, (c) exercise multiple model families, and (d) perform the preregistered per‑cluster inferential breakdown to reveal topology‑dependent effects. The archived artifacts provide exact inputs, seeds, validator rules, and provider traces needed to reproduce the pooled analysis and to perform the suggested sensitivity studies.
sections.conclusion: NetOpsTraceBench (rX4f7-1) produced a fully archived, preregistered, paired evaluation comparing one‑shot and verifier‑assisted NL→config pipelines using shared initial candidates. On 1,199 completed pairs with the requested model gpt-5-mini, pooled baseline success was 1,196/1,199 and guarded success was 1,199/1,199, yielding a paired difference of ≈0.25 percentage points (p = 0.25; 95% CI includes zero). The pooled null result is artifact‑grounded and driven by near‑ceiling baseline performance and rare repair invocation (repair = 3); the preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis H3 was not executed and therefore per‑cluster inferential claims are not supported by archived artifacts. All raw outputs, validator traces, provider audits, and analysis code are archived (see analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, execution/execution_manifest.json) to enable exact reproduction and to support sensitivity studies that vary corpus difficulty, verifier strictness, and model family.

limitations: Single model family tested (requested_model = gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across other LLMs or fine‑tuned variants.
Task corpus skew: synthetic/consented tasks yielded near‑ceiling baseline success (≈99.75%), limiting headroom and statistical power to detect practical improvements by guarded pipelines.

Emulator fidelity: Mininet‑style emulation and deterministic validators approximate production behavior but may not capture all deployment failure modes (routing convergence, vendor idiosyncrasies, transient telemetry).

Verifier configuration dependence: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acceptance thresholds and parsing rules materially affect outcomes; different verifier strictness could change repair invocation rates and measured gains.

Analytic deviation documented: the preregistration specified a Wilcoxon signed‑rank paired procedure; the archived confirmatory analysis used an exact McNemar test because outcomes were binary. This deviation is recorded in analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Preregistered per‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis (H3) was not executed; only pooled paired analysis is archived (see analysis/results.json and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Therefore per‑topology inferential claims are not supported by the archived artifacts.
